flags.hebrew: הָעֲשִׁירִים מֵהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוֹלְכִים כּוּלָּם אַחַר אֲדוֹנֵינוּ יֵשׁוּעַ
flags.note: This text appears to be from Revelation 11:15 rather than 12:1, and the content about 'the rich going after our Lord' does not match any known version of Revelation 12:1.
Uses שֶׁ relative clause where classical Hebrew would prefer a participle or construct chain. However, this is acceptable in Mishnaic Hebrew.
The word order 'a great sign in heaven - one woman' awkwardly follows Greek syntax. Natural Hebrew would be אִשָּׁה אַחַת or place the numeral more naturally.
Uses שֶׁ relative clause in temporal expression. While not impossible in late Hebrew, כְּשֶׁנּוֹלַד would be more natural.
Uses שֶׁ relative in causal clause. This construction is acceptable in Mishnaic Hebrew but shows possible Greek influence from ὅτι constructions.
Heavy use of שֶׁ relative clauses throughout the verse mirrors Greek relative clause patterns, though individually acceptable in Mishnaic Hebrew.
Uses שֶׁ + יֵשׁ construction which is standard in Mishnaic Hebrew but could reflect Greek ὅτι ἔχει patterns.
Multiple nested שֶׁ relative clauses in sequence, which while grammatically possible, creates a style more typical of translation from Greek.
Continued heavy reliance on שֶׁ relative clauses where Hebrew might prefer other constructions.
More שֶׁ relative constructions in causal and descriptive contexts.
Uses שֶׁל genitive construction which is characteristic of Mishnaic Hebrew but represents a departure from classical Hebrew construct chains.
